about: Public national emergency numbers by country of use, shown as call links on who to call (app/src/config/emergency.ts). Each number is confirmed by at least two sources of two publishers, each fetched on the date given (checkedOn), with the date the page gives itself when it has one (pageUpdated). Every medical number (samu, ambulance, emergency) has at least one national source: the telecom regulator, a ministry of the country, or the service itself. A number whose sources disagree, or that has too few sources, is left out and listed with why: no number is guessed. In each country: the medical numbers first, then the fire brigade or civil protection, then the police (listed when the file has no medical number for the country, and in Cameroon). A number marked caveat not-all-networks is said to the person as maybe not working from every network. timeZones are the IANA zones of the country in zone.tab, one country each, used to find the country of a phone offline; weakTimeZones are zones other countries may report as theirs (canonical links in the tz database), never enough alone. A country with detect false is never found from the phone, only chosen by hand.
teamCheck: TEAM CHECK: before a pilot, the team must confirm every number of the pilot country with the health authorities of the pilot district (that it answers there, from every mobile operator, free of charge), and add a number left out only once an official source gives it.
attribution: The quoted texts (says) belong to their publishers and are quoted to cite each source.
